goal.text: Does a sensory-motor neural system with adaptation as its sole mechanism, but available at various scales in spacetime, emerge neurophysiological and neuropsychological traits in its equivalent scope?
goal.falsifier: Two-sided, and both sides must be stated before this can Seal. CONFIRMED-for-now if a single-mechanism multi-scale adaptive sensorimotor model produces at least two traits it was not fit to — one neurophysiological, one neuropsychological — with the measured observable and the scale (spatial extent and time constant) reported for each. FALSIFIED if any trait in the target scope demonstrably requires a second, non-adaptive mechanism that cannot be re-expressed as adaptation at some scale. Neither outcome closes the branch; both rewrite it.
goal.successor_clause: Confirmation respawns this as a scope question — what is the boundary of the 'equivalent scope', i.e. the traits this system should NOT be expected to produce. Falsification respawns it as an inventory of the irreducible second mechanism. Either way a successor node is written before this one may be marked superseded (Conservation).
goal.adaptivity: The phrase 'sole mechanism' is the load-bearing and most fragile commitment here. If Review finds the adaptation-at-all-scales framing has quietly absorbed a second mechanism by redefinition, that is a contested finding against this node, not a clarification of it. Guard against the framing expanding to stay unfalsifiable.
